name: AI and MCP

hero.title: Your assistant learned React. This teaches it Pyreon.
hero.lede: An MCP server gives Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf or any MCP client 24 tools: the real API from each package's manifest, the compiler's verdict on a snippet, and your own routes and components. In the editor, the Reactivity Lens marks each JSX expression `live` or `static` while you type.

facts.value: 41 detector codes<small>19 React habits · 20 Pyreon mistakes · 2 native hazards</small>

items.title: The compiler grades the snippet
items.text: `explain_reactivity` runs the analysis the JSX transform uses and marks each expression live, baked once, or a footgun such as `props-destructured-body`.

items.title: The API from the source
items.text: `get_api` answers from each package's manifest: signature, usage and common mistakes. "`count.value` does not exist. Use `count()`" comes back with the answer.

items.title: React habits caught by code
items.text: `validate` returns each finding with code, line, the text as written, the fix and an auto-fixable flag. `className`, `useState` and `.map()` in JSX all have codes.

items.title: It reads your project
items.text: `get_routes`, `get_components` and `get_content_collection` read your app. `get_atlas_catalog`, `get_api_client` and `get_dependency_fabric` read Atlas, Lathe and Loom output.

after.code:
validate(Counter.tsx) → Found 5 issues:

1. react-import (line 1)          Auto-fixable: yes
   Fix: import { ... } from "@pyreon/core"
2. props-destructured (line 3)    Auto-fixable: no
   Fix: (props: Props) => /* read props.x directly */
3. use-state (line 4)             Auto-fixable: yes
   Fix: count = signal(start)
4. use-effect-deps (line 5)       Auto-fixable: yes
   Fix: effect(() => { /* reads are auto-tracked */ })
5. class-name-prop (line 6)       Auto-fixable: yes
   Fix: class="btn"

demo.title: Watch the tools answer.
demo.text: Pick a question. Each answer is real output from the server on this snippet, recorded over stdio and trimmed to fit.
demo.referenceHtml:
ask
tool calls
demo.spec: Same layout as the reference: a column of four question buttons (aria-pressed on the active one) and a log panel that prints lines one by one, 380 ms apart. The four questions and their logs are replaced with real tool output: explain_reactivity on a component that destructures props in its body (2 live, 1 baked-static, 1 footgun); validate on a list rendered with .map() (array-map-jsx); validate on a click handler that calls count(count() + 1) (props-destructured, signal-write-as-call); get_api for reactivity/signal. The first question runs on load.

features.title: What's in the server, and around it.

items.name: validate
items.text: React-habit, Pyreon-misuse and native-hazard detectors in one call, sorted by line. It says when the native checks were skipped.

items.name: explain_reactivity

items.text: a paged index of the whole catalog (522 entries on main); ask by name or category, or pass `full: true` for every entry in full.

items.name: diagnose and explain_error
items.text: paste an error message into `diagnose` for the likely Pyreon cause, the fix and a code sample; `explain_error` reads a dev error report with its reactive trace.

items.name: migrate_react
items.text: a first pass over React code: hooks to signals and effects, `className` to `class`, imports swapped, with a list of changes.

api.title: 24 tools, and the pieces around them.

limits.title: It needs an MCP client
limits.text: Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf and other MCP clients call the tools. A plain chat window cannot; give it `llms.txt` instead.

limits.title: Tools are listed lean
limits.text: `tools/list` carries names and parameter schemas without prose, so every session starts small (about 8 KB). If your assistant picks the wrong tool, ask it to call `mcp_overview` first.

limits.title: migrate_react is a first pass
limits.text: It turns `useState` into `signal()` but leaves setter calls like `setCount(n)` and plain reads like `count` as written, so its output does not run as is. Rewrite them as `count.set(n)` and `count()`, then type-check before you commit.

limits.title: Native checks are optional
limits.text: The two native-hazard codes, for the experimental iOS and Android targets, need `@pyreon/native-compiler` installed. Without it, `validate` still runs the other 39 codes, and on a snippet that imports `@pyreon/primitives` it says the native checks were skipped.

limits.title: The Lens is structural
limits.text: It tells you whether an expression will update. To see how often it did, use Live Program Inlay Hints, served by the same LSP.

recipes.title: Connect Claude Code
recipes.text: Put this in `.mcp.json` at the project root. Cursor reads the same shape from `.cursor/mcp.json`, and Windsurf takes the same `mcpServers` block in its MCP config. `pyreon mcp` starts the same server from the CLI.

recipes.title: Start a project that already knows its assistant
recipes.text: The scaffolder writes the AI files for the tools you name. Leave `--ai` out and it preselects `.mcp.json` and `CLAUDE.md` (the default with `--yes`).
recipes.code:
npm create @pyreon/zero@latest my-app -- --ai mcp,claude,cursor --yes

# .mcp.json               (the server above)
# CLAUDE.md                (Pyreon rules for Claude Code)
# .cursor/rules/pyreon.md  (the same for Cursor)

recipes.title: Give your own docs an llms.txt
recipes.text: Building docs with `@pyreon/zero-content`? Turn on `seo.llms` next to `seo.baseUrl` and the build writes `dist/llms.txt`, with one line per page.

faq.q: Does my code leave my machine?
faq.a: Not through this server. It runs locally over stdio and makes no network calls; tools read the snippet your assistant passes and the files in your project. Your assistant's own model provider is a separate question.

faq.q: How much of my context window does it use?
faq.a: The tool list is about 8 KB of JSON. `get_anti_patterns` returns a compact index (its first page is about 35 KB of text); the full catalog, over 300 KB, comes back only when the assistant asks with `full: true`.

No. `analyzeReactivity` runs the reactive-or-static analysis the JSX transform uses to decide what to bind, and both compiler backends (Rust and JS) emit the same span data. `explain_reactivity` gives your assistant the same verdicts.
Any editor that speaks LSP inlay hints: register `pyreon-lint --lsp` for `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js` and `.jsx`. For VS Code, symlink the extension from the Pyreon repo's `packages/tools/lint/vscode`.

faq.q: My assistant does not speak MCP. Now what?
faq.a: Hand it `llms.txt` (a short index) or `llms-full.txt` (every package's section). Both are generated from the same manifests as `get_api`. `create-zero --ai copilot` writes `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
